provider.name: Darwin Core Archive
provider.organization_type: biodiversity data exchange packaging standard and implementation ecosystem
provider.description: Darwin Core Archive is a biodiversity data exchange format that packages one core data table, optional extension tables, a meta.xml descriptor, and dataset-level metadata—commonly EML—inside a portable archive. It is widely used for occurrence, checklist, sampling-event, multimedia, measurement, and related biodiversity datasets.

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting Darwin Core Archive documentation, Darwin Core terms, archive structure, EML metadata rules, core and extension schemas, validation, publishing tools, controlled vocabularies, licensing, citation, and implementation guidance.
purpose.authoritative_notice: TDWG remains authoritative for Darwin Core and Darwin Core Archive specifications. GBIF, EML, and other implementation sources remain authoritative for their respective schemas, registries, tools, publishing guidance, and terms.

notes: Darwin Core Archive is primarily a file packaging and metadata standard, not a network API.
Machine-readable schemas, term URIs, extension registries, validators, and repositories should be treated as supporting resources.
Do not infer a public API where only static standard documents or registry files exist.
Capture exact file formats, namespaces, row types, schema versions, and validation behavior.

optional_files: one or more extension data files
notes: Verify exact registered row type URIs and schema versions before use.
Preserve declared delimiter, quote, escape, encoding, and header settings from meta.xml.
Do not assume all archives use occurrence.txt or tab-separated UTF-8 files.
Do not infer extension linkage from row order; use declared identifiers.
Separate rights for the standard, schemas, archive package, dataset metadata, records, media, and software.
Preserve rights, license, accessRights, rightsHolder, bibliographicCitation, and source fields.
Do not assume Darwin Core compliance grants permission to redistribute the enclosed data.
Do not assume an archive-level license overrides more restrictive media or third-party records.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some anchors, registry filenames, schema versions, and GBIF core definitions may change; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Darwin Core Archive is a packaging standard, not a single centralized data provider.
Do not recursively crawl every term, extension, vocabulary, GitHub issue, or IPT resource when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store passwords, API keys, cookies, OAuth tokens, publisher credentials, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Always preserve namespace URIs, term URIs, row types, schema versions, meta.xml settings, archive checksums, licenses, and source provenance.
